instruction: Navigate to slide 5 and change the font color of the title text to red.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to slide 5, selected 2 shapes, opened Format > Character > Font Effects, set font color to #FFFF00 via custom color picker, but the color change did not properly apply to all text runs. Final screenshot shows text still in original green color.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate between slides in LibreOffice Impress, select objects with Ctrl+A, open Format > Character dialog, navigate Font Effects tab, use custom color picker with hex values, save files with Ctrl+S
metadata.failure_analysis: Model selected shapes and applied color via Character dialog, but the font color change did not persist in the saved file. Likely the color was applied at shape level but not propagated to individual text runs, or the selection did not properly include all text content.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to changing font color of only the title textbox (not all textboxes) to red, reducing scope to a single shape. Model demonstrated the full workflow for color change.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to slide 5 and changing the title text font color to red (#FF0000). Getter extracts font color of text runs in slide 5 shape 3 (the title). Metric checks all runs match expected color with partial credit.

scoring_breakdown.font_color: 1.0 - All text runs in title shape have color #FF0000 (partial credit per run)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads pptx file from VM, accesses slide index 4 (slide 5, 0-based), and extracts font colors from all text runs in the specified shape.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter — accesses expected.get('expected_color') directly from the rules dict, which is correct for type='rule'.
Expected color 'FF0000' is semantically correct for red.
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.
Partial credit scoring (matching runs / total runs) is reasonable for this task.
Minor concern: shape_index=3 is hardcoded as the title shape. Standard PPTX layouts typically have titles at index 0 or 1; index 3 may be incorrect depending on the file's actual shape ordering.
Minor concern: text runs with inherited/theme colors (no explicit RGB) return None and count toward the denominator, potentially reducing the score even if the title visually appears red.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider identifying the title shape by its placeholder type (e.g., PP_PLACEHOLDER.TITLE) rather than a hardcoded shape_index, which would be more robust across different slide layouts.
Consider filtering out None color values from the denominator, or treating inherited colors separately, to avoid penalizing runs that may not have explicit RGB set.
